originalTitle: Trump dismisses concerns about USS Abraham Lincoln, saying its record-breaking 250 days at sea ‘not nearly enough’ – live
summary: President claims families not worried, despite relatives raising concerns, but confirms USS George Washington will replace aircraft carrier on Iran mission
content: Bulldozers have begun plowing up ground at the mouth of Big Bend national park’s famed Santa Elena Canyon as part of the Trump administration’s multibillion-dollar “smart wall” expansion on the US-Mexico border, according to new footage taken by activists who have been monitoring the site. Tensions have run high since the Trump administration announced plans to erect new border security infrastructure in the roughly 500-mile Big Bend region of south-west Texas, which includes the Lone Star State’s largest and most-visited national park. Since last week, activists have shared video footage that appeared to show heavy machinery laying the groundwork for new border infrastructure that US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) did not announce and initially denied was happening. By Thursday, photographer Natalie Newman captured video footage of bulldozers plowing earth at the mouth of the Santa Elena Canyon, a frequently visited stretch of the Rio Grande flanked by 1,500ft cliffs. “It’s just devastating,” said Laiken Jordahl, a public lands advocate with the Center for Biological Diversity. “They’re bulldozing a brand new road through the most beloved stretch of the park.” Democratic lawmakers have continued to criticize the Trump administration’s response to reports of distress on the USS Abraham Lincoln Adam Schiff, the California senator wrote on X: “Listen to what Trump said about servicemembers suffering a lengthy deployment onboard the USS Abraham Lincoln… He said they have not been deployed ‘nearly long enough.’ Easy to say when you spend your time golfing at Mar-a-Lago.” Ruben Gallego of Arizona wrote: “Cadet Bone Spurs thinks he understands what happens on deployments,” making referene to the president’s 1968 medical draft exemption for bone spurs in his heels, which excused him from service during the Vietnam War. On his way to New York earlier on Friday, Donald Trump approached reporters with a copy of a news headline he wanted them to see. Holding up a print-out of the headline, “Prescription drug prices record sharpest drop in more than 60 years”, the president waved the print-out around and encouraged the press pool to record and photograph it. “The headline today is exactly that,” he said proudly. “Did you see it?” He then read the good news aloud and held up the print-out again, which displayed the headline and the first five lines of the article, for the cameras. “Okay, got it? Everybody have it?” he asked. What the president did not explain is that the text of the article, published by the Washington Post on Thursday, reported that while the Trump White House “took credit for” the biggest year-over-year drop in drug prices in more than 60 years in July, independent experts “said a Biden-era policy that requires Medicare to negotiate prices for some popular prescription drugs is more likely to be driving down costs.” “The Inflation Reduction Act was a signature accomplishment of former president Joe Biden, a sprawling measure enacted in 2022 that aimed to lower prescription drug prices by requiring Medicare, the federal health program for the elderly, to begin negotiating the prices it pays drugmakers for an array of popular and costly prescription drugs,” the Post’s report noted. “The first price reductions took effect at the beginning of this year.” The Post also quoted Richard Frank, a professor emeritus of health economics at Harvard University, expressing doubt Trump’s policies were behind the drop in drug prices. “If I was a betting guy on what mattered most, it would be probably stuff around the Inflation Reduction Act,” Frank said, adding that Trump’s efforts “wouldn’t be where I’d place my money.” A federal court in Nevada dismissed the Department of Justice’s case seeking to compel states to turn over their unredacted voter rolls. The court was the 22nd consecutive court to reject the Trump administration’s campaign to obtain private data in its efforts to find evidence of voter fraud. The administration has not found any substantial evidence of fraud, and critics and election experts have said the effort to obtain voter information is another attempt to sow distrust in the system. The DOJ has sued sued 30 states and Washington DC to try to force secretaries of state to hand over the data. On Friday, US district judge Anne Traum said she was “joining every other court to have addressed the issue so far” in her ruling. Here’s more background on the administration’s effort, and why even red states are pushing back: The acting secretary of the navy, Hung Cao, again denied poor conditions and a mental health crisis on board USS Abraham Lincoln. “The USS Abraham Lincoln crushed their deployment and will return home soon as part of a planned rotation,” Cao said in a post on X. “Unfortunately, the media are trying to paint our warriors as victims.” Here’s more from my colleague Edward Pilkington, who reported on the crisis aboard the aircraft carrier: Two leading specialist military papers, the Navy Times and Stars and Stripes, are reporting that there have been multiple attempts by sailors to jump overboard as poor conditions and mental stresses on the Lincoln reach the breaking point. The crew is in its ninth month at sea, and has spent 250 days consecutively without making land – a record for an aircraft carrier in modern times. Worried families vented their anxieties about loved ones onboard the Lincoln at an emotional town hall meeting with navy leaders in San Diego last Thursday, Stars and Stripes reported. One spouse among the 200 or so family members said that her husband had texted her that day saying “he hopes he doesn’t wake up tomorrow”. The families’ worries were expressed directly to navy leadership, represented at the town hall by the acting navy secretary, Hung Cao, and other top officials. A woman at the meeting told Cao that the navy had “broken trust between us and the leadership”, the paper reported. The Navy Times gave details of thwarted suicide attempt

chineseSummary: 总统声称家人并不担心，尽管亲属提出了担忧，但确认乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰将取代航空母舰执行伊朗任务
chineseContent: 根据一直监视该地点的活动人士拍摄的新镜头，推土机已开始在大本德国家公园著名的圣埃琳娜峡谷口犁地，这是特朗普政府耗资数十亿美元在美墨边境扩建“智能墙”的一部分。自从特朗普政府宣布计划在德克萨斯州西南部约 500 英里的大本德地区建立新的边境安全基础设施以来，紧张局势一直处于高度紧张状态，该地区包括孤星州最大、访问量最大的国家公园。自上周以来，活动人士分享的视频片段似乎显示重型机械正在为新的边境基础设施奠定基础，而美国海关和边境保护局（CBP）并未宣布这一点，并且最初否认正在发生这种情况。周四，摄影师娜塔莉·纽曼 (Natalie Newman) 拍摄了推土机在圣埃琳娜峡谷 (Santa Elena Canyon) 河口犁土的视频片段，这是格兰德河 (Rio Grande) 的一个经常参观的河段，两侧是 1,500 英尺高的悬崖。 “这简直是毁灭性的，”生物多样性中心的公共土地倡导者莱肯·乔达尔说。 “他们正在用推土机推平一条穿过公园最受欢迎的路段的全新道路。”加州参议员亚当·希夫 (Adam Schiff) 在 X 上写道，民主党议员继续批评特朗普政府对亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰遇险报告的反应：“听听特朗普关于在亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰上长期部署的军人的说法……他说他们的部署时间‘几乎不够长’。当你在海湖庄园打高尔夫球时，这句话很容易说出来。”亚利桑那州的鲁本·加莱戈 (Ruben Gallego) 写道：“学员骨刺认为他了解部署时会发生什么”，这指的是总统 1968 年针对脚后跟骨刺的医疗草案豁免，
